notes:
Extract zips: finished .zip, .tar and .tar.gz downloads get an Extract button that unpacks them into a folder next to the file. In Settings you can have Laneway ask you, or extract automatically and delete the zip afterwards. Nothing is ever overwritten.
New installer: a cleaner, one-click installer in Laneway's own style, with a matching uninstaller.
The Laneway extension is now on the Chrome Web Store. The "Get the browser extension" button takes you straight to it, and Laneway works with the store version in Chrome and Edge.

Power button: turn Laneway on or off in your browser with one click in the extension.
Skip this site: leave a site's downloads to the browser. Right-click "Download with Laneway" still works there.
Live progress in your browser: the extension shows what's downloading, with pause, resume, open and show-in-folder buttons.
Download all: the extension lists every file on the page you're on. Filter by videos, music, archives and more, tick what you want and send them all to Laneway.
Done notifications: your browser tells you when a download it sent to Laneway finishes, with Open and Show in folder buttons.

No right-click needed: with the browser extension, just click a link to a video, song, zip or installer and it goes to Laneway, even if the browser would normally open it in a tab. Ctrl+click still opens a link in the browser.
Get the browser extension: a new button at the top of Laneway shows you how to add the extension to Chrome or Edge.

Browser extension: with the Laneway extension for Chrome and Edge, your browser downloads go straight to Laneway, even ones that need you to be signed in. Set it up in Settings.
Connection details: click any download to see each connection: which part of the file it's fetching, how much it has downloaded, its speed and any retries. Plus average and top speed, time spent and more.
Picks up where it stopped: if your internet drops, Laneway keeps retrying and carries on from where it stopped. Downloads interrupted by closing Laneway, a crash or a power cut carry on next time it opens.
Safer resuming: if the file on the server changes between attempts, Laneway notices and starts it over instead of producing a broken file.
Tabs and search: sort your list into Active, Paused, Finished and Failed, or search by name.

New name: FastDL is now Laneway. Same app, same downloads and settings, just a new name.
Its own window: Laneway opens in its own window with its own icon on the taskbar, so you can pin it and spot it easily.
Taskbar alerts: when a download finishes while Laneway is in the background, its taskbar button flashes.
Dark title bar when Windows is set to dark mode.
What's new screen: after each update, Laneway shows you what changed, like this. You can find it again any time in Settings.

Automatic updates: Laneway now keeps itself up to date. Your downloads are paused and saved while it updates, then carry on.
Smarter speed: connections that finish early help out slower ones, so the last few percent don't drag.
Download queue: choose how many files download at once in Settings. The rest wait in line.
Speed limit: cap Laneway's total speed so browsing and calls stay smooth.
Change link: if a download link expires, paste a fresh one and keep your progress.
Notifications when a download finishes or fails, and your PC stays awake while downloading.

Paste or drop several links at once.
Open finished files straight from Laneway.
Pause all and Resume all buttons.
Clearer error messages.
First release (as FastDL): multi-connection downloads, pause and resume, and a Windows installer.
